summary: Proceed only after a required change: Source A (bulk row-owner kernel, pooler m==1) can be ported as specified once state['bulk_route_hit'] is dropped. Source B's per-call save/set/restore of torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library is forbidden by standing policy and MUST be replaced by a prepare-time cuBLASLt plan held in state (reuse the bf16-cublaslt-algo-pick-in-prepare-m128-m256 load_inline extension), forced to the no-split-K 48x64 algo; if prepare cannot reproduce that algo, drop cell B and ship A alone.
justification: A. Source A is plausible and well evidenced. pooler decode_1 is a 67.1 MB pure weight stream with a 14.0 us floor. In job 571ea532 the bulk_kernel<32,8192,8,0> ran at 17.0 us (~3.95 TB/s), while master's _bf16_swapab_kernel runs at 18.7 us (FINDINGS, check 85c91578). Paired 1.226x vs 1.135x is about 8%, well outside the ~1.5% row noise. Restricting it to m==1 matches that run's own losses at m>=8/16/32. Source B's mechanism is real but fragile. With the toggle, qkv_gate verify_16 launched one nvjet_sm90_tst_48x64_64x15_4x2_h_bz_TNN (16.2 us) and dropped the 12.7 us split-K kernel plus the 3.0 us splitKreduce node, so the 1.068x vs 0.998x row is attributable. WEAKEST LINK: that algo came from torch's Lt path running under torch's small Lt workspace, which excludes the split-K candidates. The policy-compliant prepare-time route has already been tried. bf16-cublaslt-algo-pick-in-prepare-m128-m256 (job 26a8be34, log lines 6-14) asked the Lt heuristic with a 32 MiB workspace and got 8 qkv_gate m=128 candidates, ALL split-K (splitK 2-6, red=2). It picked cand 3 and the row came out flat (16.81 -> 16.49, 1.0095). A naive port of that extension therefore will NOT reproduce the 48x64 no-split-K kernel. The plan must set CUBLASLT_MATMUL_PREF_MAX_WORKSPACE_BYTES to 0 or to torch's Lt workspace size, or enumerate AlgoGetIds/ConfigSetAttribute with SPLITK_NUM=1, and assert in prepare that the chosen algo has splitK=1. A second weakness is the expected magnitude. The master qkv verify_16 row has drifted between 16.8 and 17.4 us across runs, so the realistic gain is -3% to -6%, not a firm -6%. The headline expectation (+0.8%, ~1.25) is inside the CI and cannot by itself confirm or refute anything. CONJECTURE (additive, no interaction): justified. The two cells are in different loads and different captured graphs, and every other cell is byte-identical master. The run CAN test it per cell: PATH CHOSEN lines, the gate medians, the asserted kernel names, and the per-row paired ratios against the source runs (pooler d1 ~1.22x, qkv v16 ~1.06x, +-2%). The 'Lt preference leaks into the next captured cell' refutation clause becomes moot once the toggle is replaced. Keep the replacement check: qkv_gate verify_32 must still launch master's nvjet, and no other (layer, m) may show a cublasLt run.
confounders: pooler-nn-layout-widen-m256 / restack-three-cell-wins (NN layout gated at m=65..256): they touch the pooler weights (state['pooler_t']) but not m==1. The bulk repack adds a third 67 MB copy of W_pooler per state, so watch HBM/L2 placement effects only as drift. No functional interaction.

bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton / bf16-restack-m16-swapab (master's _bf16_swapab_kernel at pooler m<=32): this is the incumbent that A replaces at m==1 only. The bulk branch must be checked BEFORE the swapab16 branch, as specified. If the branch order is wrong, the cell silently stays master and the PATH CHOSEN/kernel-name assert must catch it.

sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity (_bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl at qkv_gate m=128): this is the incumbent that B replaces, and it acts as the control rather than a confounder. The replacement Lt plan must time against exactly this call in its gate.

restack-three-cell-wins (ouns/router cluster extensions built at import): the third import-time extension build adds ~37-40 s of compile, plus ~15 s for the Lt load_inline. This affects only the time budget, not the timed rows.
interference: No companion is warranted, and none is worth a scored run. The two changed cells are in different loads and graphs, and every other cell runs byte-identical master code. Each changed cell carries its own attribution: a PATH CHOSEN line with candidate and master medians, plus a torch.profiler assertion of the launched kernel (bulk_kernel<32,8192,8,0>; a single nvjet 48x64 with no splitKreduce). That attribution makes both a gain and a loss interpretable per row without an ab-revert or a control. A per-source control would only re-measure what 571ea532 and 5ed9ace1 already measured. If B's prepare-time plan cannot find a splitK=1 algo, B prints PATH CHOSEN master and the run degenerates to A alone, which is still interpretable.
rules_flags: STANDING POLICY (blocking for cell B as written): the per-call save/set/restore of torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library('cublaslt') in kernel_fn is per-call mutation of process-global state. A pass of the judge's static check in 5ed9ace1 does not change our policy. Required: replace it with a prepare-time cuBLASLt plan held in state. Port the load_inline extension from muse_bf16_proj/hypotheses/done/neutral/bf16-cublaslt-algo-pick-in-prepare-m128-m256.patch: descriptors keyed by shape, a 64-byte algo row and a workspace tensor in state, and one cublasLtMatmul on the current stream in kernel_fn. Restrict it to (qkv_gate, m==128, n==2304). Constrain the heuristic or algo to splitK=1 (workspace pref 0 or torch's Lt default size, or ConfigSetAttribute SPLITK_NUM=1), assert splitK=1 and the 48x64 tile in the prepare printout, and keep the <=0.98 graph-replay gate. If no such algo is found or the gate fails, DROP cell B (route master). Do not fall back to the toggle.
EXTRA: the source's state['bulk_route_hit'] = (layer, m) write in _bulk_forward must be dropped. kernel_fn must write nothing to state or to module globals per call.
Bulk kernel error word: if the device kernel writes an error word, zero it once in prepare(). Never reset or read it on the host per call (no .item() in kernel_fn).
Repack: _bulk_repack must be a lossless bf16 permutation of W_pooler. Keep the bit-exact round-trip assertion in prepare() and never store any other precision.
Gate correctness check: the probe-row bound (rel <= 1e-4) is stricter than the judge's 0.1%, which is fine. The gate uses synthetic x only and no data-derived caching.

Budget: three import-time CUDA builds (~37 s each) plus the ~15 s Lt load_inline sit inside the 10-minute run limit. Make sure the import-time builds also respect it if the judge imports more than once (two states).
open_questions: Which workspace size does torch's Lt path pass on this image (CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE / at::cuda::getCUDABlasLtWorkspaceSize)? Matching it should reproduce the 48x64 no-split-K heuristic result 0 exactly.
Does the 48x64 no-split-K algo stay bit-identical in error to the incumbent (rel vs fp64 ~1.66e-3)? Keep the algo-pick extension's 1.10x-of-incumbent fp64 guard.

Is the bulk extension built once per process (shared by both judge states) with per-state repacked weights, as the change says? Confirm that no module-global device pointer is captured into the graph.

Simpler alternative if the extension is unwanted: torch.addmm(zero_bias_bf16_in_state, x, W.t()) takes torch's cublasLt gemm_and_bias path without touching the global preference. Its algo choice is unverified, so it would need the same gate and kernel-name assert.
